paragraphs: Friend, here is the big idea: Jesus is what God promised all along, and the forgiveness of sins comes through Him. Paul starts way back with the fathers, Egypt, the judges and the kings, because every bit of it was pointing to one place. "From the descendants of this man, God has brought to Israel the Savior Jesus, as He promised" (Acts 13:23). God keeps His promises, and He keeps them in ways people don't see coming.

Now hear the headline, because it's for YOU. "Through Him everyone who believes is justified from everything from which you could not be justified by the law of Moses" (Acts 13:39). David served God's purpose and fell asleep, and his body saw decay, but the One God raised did not (Acts 13:36-37). That is why you don't have to earn your way in, friend, you believe and receive. I spent years in a junk drawer thinking I was past fixing, and I'm telling you, grace is not something you bake your way into.

The message also comes with a choice, and Paul doesn't hide it. Some in Pisidian Antioch contradicted him, and the Gentiles "rejoiced and glorified the word of the Lord" (Acts 13:48). Even when Paul and Barnabas were driven out, "the disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit" (Acts 13:52). So don't let a hard crowd steal your joy, baker. Hold on to the good news, keep your ovens ready, and let the joy rise.
